notes: ANG-form (subject/topic) of 'I'. Set: ako (ang) / ko (ng) / akin (sa). Comes after the predicate: 'Pagod ako.'

examples.taglish: Pagod na ako, grabe ang traffic.

examples.en: I'll be the one to pay.

notes: NG-form of 'I': possessor ('kotse ko' = my car) or actor of an object-focus verb ('Binili ko' = I bought it). Never starts a sentence.
SA-form of 'I'. 'sa akin' = to/for me; 'akin ito' = this is mine. Often said 'sa'kin'.
ANG-form of 'you' used at the START of a sentence or standing alone; after the predicate use 'ka'. Set: ikaw/ka (ang) / mo (ng) / iyo (sa).
Enclitic ANG-form of 'you'; goes right after the first word of the predicate: 'Saan ka?' 'Okay ka lang?' Use 'ikaw' at sentence start.
NG-form of 'you': 'bag mo' = your bag; 'Kinain mo?' = Did you eat it? Also softens commands: 'Buksan mo.'
SA-form of 'you'. Almost always 'sa iyo', pronounced and texted 'sa'yo'. 'Iyo na' = it's yours now.

examples.tl: Sa iyo ba ang jacket na ito?

notes: ANG-form; gender-neutral (he or she). Set: siya (ang) / niya (ng) / kanya (sa). Texted 'sya'. Not used for things ('it' is ito/iyon or dropped).

examples.en: He/she is still at the office.

en: his / her / by him or her
notes: NG-form of siya: 'bahay niya' = his/her house; 'Sinabi niya' = he/she said. Texted 'nya'.

en: his / hers / to him or her
notes: SA-form of siya; usually 'sa kanya'. 'Kanya ito' = this is his/hers. Formal spelling 'kaniya'.

examples.tl: Ibinigay ko sa kanya ang resibo.

notes: EXCLUSIVE 'we' = me and others, NOT the listener. Set: kami / namin / amin. Compare tayo (includes you).
NG-form of kami (exclusive). 'condo namin' = our condo (not yours). 'Kinain namin' = we ate it.
SA-form of kami. 'sa amin' also means 'at our place/hometown': 'Sa amin, walang traffic.'

examples.tl: Pumunta ka sa amin sa Sabado.
examples.en: Come to our place on Saturday.

examples.tl: Sa amin sa probinsya, mas mura ang isda.
examples.en: Back home in the province, fish is cheaper.

notes: INCLUSIVE 'we' = me + you. After a verb root it means 'let's': 'Kain tayo!' Set: tayo / natin / atin.
NG-form of tayo (inclusive). 'Order natin' = let's order it. 'bayan natin' = our country (yours and mine).
SA-form of tayo. 'sa atin' = to us / here in our place (incl. you): 'Mahal ang gas sa atin.'

examples.en: This is for all of us.

examples.tl: Sa atin sa Pilipinas, lagi may rice.
examples.en: Here in the Philippines, there's always rice.

notes: ANG-form plural 'you'. Also POLITE singular to elders/strangers: 'Saan po kayo?' Set: kayo / ninyo / inyo.

examples.en: Where did you come from, sir/ma'am?

notes: NG-form of kayo; spoken/texted 'niyo' or 'nyo'. Also polite singular: 'Ano po ang order niyo?'
SA-form of kayo. 'sa inyo' = to you all / at your place. Polite: 'Para sa inyo po.'

examples.tl: Pupunta kami sa inyo sa Linggo.
examples.en: We'll come to your place on Sunday.

examples.tl: Sa inyo na lang yung natira.
examples.en: You guys just keep the leftovers.

notes: ANG-form 'they'. Set: sila / nila / kanila. Also polite singular in some contexts ('sila' for a respected person).

examples.en: They were the ones who invited me.

notes: NG-form of sila. 'bahay nila' = their house; 'Ginawa nila' = they did it. Also used for 'X and company': 'kina/sila Ana'.
SA-form of sila; usually 'sa kanila' = to them / at their place.

examples.tl: Sabihin mo sa kanila na late ako.

examples.en: We'll eat at their place later.

notes: Replaces 'ko ikaw' (I = actor, you = object) in one word: 'Mahal kita' = I love you. 'Tawagan kita' = I'll call you.

examples.en: I'll pick you up at the mall.
examples.taglish: Susunduin kita sa Glorietta, wait ka lang.

notes: Demonstrative, near the speaker. Spoken/texted 'to': 'Ano to?' NG-form: nito. Location: dito.
Demonstrative, near the LISTENER. Almost always spoken 'yan'. NG-form: niyan. Location: diyan.
Demonstrative, far from both. Spoken 'yun'. Linked form 'yung' (iyong) works like 'the': 'yung bag ko'. NG-form: niyon/noon. Location: doon.

examples.en: Get my bag (that bag of mine).

notes: Location near speaker. 'Dito lang' = just here. 'Taga-dito' = from here. Spelling 'rito' after a vowel is formal.

examples.en: I'm just here at the condo.

notes: Location near listener. Texted 'dyan' or 'jan'. 'Nandiyan' = it's there with you. 'Diyan lang' = right there.

examples.en: Put it there on the table.

notes: Location far from both. Spoken 'dun'. 'Nandoon/nandun' = it's over there. 'Doon tayo kumain.'

examples.en: Let's eat over there in Poblacion.

notes: 'In this manner'. Often opens an explanation: 'Ganito kasi...' = Here's the thing...

examples.tl: Ganito kasi, na-cancel ang flight ko.
examples.en: Here's the thing, my flight got cancelled.

notes: 'Like that (what you're doing/have)'. 'Huwag ganyan' = don't be like that. 'Ganyan talaga' = that's how it is.

examples.tl: Ganyan talaga sa Manila, traffic lagi.
examples.en: That's just how Manila is, always traffic.

notes: Spoken 'ganun'. 'Ganun ba?' = Oh, is that so? 'Ganun talaga' = that's life. Very common reaction word.

examples.tl: Ganun ba? Hindi ko alam yun.
examples.en: Is that so? I didn't know that.
That's just how it is, nothing we can do.

notes: NG-form of ito: 'presyo nito' = the price of this. Also 'recently': 'kamakailan lang nito'.

examples.en: How much is the price of this?

notes: NG-form of iyan. 'Ano ang lasa niyan?' = What does that taste like? Spoken 'nyan'.
NG-form of iyon, but mostly used as 'back then / at that time'. 'Noong' before a time word: 'noong Lunes' = last Monday.

examples.en: Back then, fares were still cheap.

notes: Presentative 'here (is)'. Spoken 'eto'. 'Eto na' = here it comes / here you go. 'Eto, o' when handing something over.
Presentative 'there (near you)'. Also 'See? Told you.' or 'There you go' when something happens as expected.

examples.tl: Ayan, dumating na ang order mo.

examples.en: See! I told you it would rain.

notes: Presentative 'there (far)'. Pointing: 'Ayun, o!' Also a filler meaning 'so, yeah, that's it': 'Ayun, umuwi na lang ako.'

examples.tl: Ayun, late na kami, kaya di na kami pumunta.
examples.en: So yeah, we were late, so we didn't go anymore.

notes: 'Ano ito?' = What is this? Also a filler for a word you can't recall ('yung ano...') and a tag: '..., ano?' (right?).

examples.en: What do you want to eat?

notes: 'Sino siya?' Plural form 'sino-sino'. NG form: 'nino' (rare); SA form: 'kanino'.

examples.en: Who was the one who called?

notes: 'Where' with verbs: 'Saan ka pupunta?' For 'where IS something', use 'nasaan'. 'Taga-saan ka?' = Where are you from?
'Where is (a thing/person)?' Answer with nasa / nandito / nandiyan / nandoon. Casual 'Asan?'
Spoken 'kelan'. 'Kailan ka uuwi?' Future or past. 'Kailan pa?' = since when?

examples.en: When are you coming back to Manila?

notes: Answer usually starts with 'Kasi...'. 'Bakit naman?' = But why? 'Bakit hindi?' = Why not?
Spoken 'pano'. 'Paano pumunta sa...' = How to get to... 'Paano kung...' = What if...

examples.tl: Paano pumunta sa Ayala mula dito?
examples.en: How do I get to Ayala from here?

notes: 'Ilan kayo?' = How many are you? Also 'a few': 'ilang araw' = a few days. Linker: 'ilang'.

examples.en: How many are you (in the group)?
How many hours is the trip?

notes: Only for prices. For amount/degree use 'gaano'. 'Magkano lahat?' = How much in total?

examples.tl: Magkano ang isang kilo ng mangga?
examples.en: How much is a kilo of mangoes?

notes: 'Alin ang gusto mo?' = Which do you want? Plural 'alin-alin'.
SA-form of sino. 'Kanino ito?' = Whose is this? 'Kay' + name answers it: 'Kay Ana.'

examples.en: To whom did you give it?

notes: Degree question used with ka- adjectives: 'Gaano kalayo?' = How far? 'Gaano katagal?' = How long?

examples.tl: Gaano kalayo ang airport mula dito?
examples.en: How far is the airport from here?

notes: From Spanish 'como esta'. 'Kumusta ka?' Also 'Kumusta ang trabaho?' = How's work? Casual 'Musta?'
Marks the sentence topic/subject (ANG-phrase). 'Masarap ang adobo.' Also for exclamations: 'Ang ganda!' = So pretty!

examples.en: Grab is so expensive right now!

notes: Pronounced 'nang'. Marks possessor ('bahay ng kaibigan ko') or indefinite object ('Bumili ako ng tubig'). Not the same as 'nang' (adverb linker).

examples.tl: Ito ang bahay ng kaibigan ko.

notes: All-purpose location/direction marker; also future time ('sa Lunes' = on Monday) and definite object with some verbs.

examples.tl: Pupunta ako sa Makati sa Lunes.
examples.en: I'm going to Makati on Monday.

notes: ANG-marker for personal names: 'Si Ana ang boss.' Plural 'sina' (Ana and others). Set: si / ni / kay.
NG-marker for names: 'kotse ni Ana' = Ana's car; 'Binili ni Ana' = Ana bought it. Plural 'nina'.
SA-marker for names: 'Ibigay mo kay Ana' = Give it to Ana. 'kay Ana' also = at Ana's. Plural 'kina'.
Pronounced 'manga'. Pluralizes nouns: 'mga tao' = people. Before numbers/times = 'around': 'mga alas-7' = about 7.

examples.tl: Marami ang mga tao sa mall.
examples.en: There are a lot of people at the mall.

notes: Joins modifier + noun. After a vowel/n: -ng ('malaking bahay'); after a consonant: 'na' ('masarap na ulam'). Not the 'na' meaning 'already'.

examples.tl: Masarap na ulam at malamig na beer.

examples.en: The man in white is the driver.

notes: Lets the topic come first: 'Ako ay pagod' = I am tired. Formal/written; speech prefers 'Pagod ako'. Also an exclamation 'Ay!' = Oh!

examples.tl: Ang Pilipinas ay may mahigit 7,000 isla.
Ay! Nakalimutan ko ang wallet ko.

en: is at / is in / is on
notes: na + sa = 'is located at'. 'Nasa bahay ako' = I'm at home. Answers 'Nasaan?'. With names: 'nakay' (rare).

examples.tl: Nasa bahay lang ako buong araw.
examples.en: I was just at home all day.
The key is on the table.

notes: Plural of si: 'sina Ana at Marco' = Ana and Marco; 'sina Ana' alone = Ana and her group. NG: nina. SA: kina.

examples.tl: Dumating na sina Ana at Marco.

notes: Plural of kay. 'kina Ana' = at Ana's place / to Ana and company. Very common for 'at X's house'.

examples.en: We're going to Ana's place later.

examples.tl: Ibigay mo kina Marco ang susi.
examples.en: Give the key to Marco and them.

notes: Enclitic: change of state ('Tapos na' = done already). With commands = 'now/go ahead': 'Kain na.' Opposite of 'pa'.

examples.en: Let's go now, we're already late.

notes: Enclitic: ongoing state ('Nasa office pa siya'), 'not yet' with hindi/wala ('Hindi pa'), or 'more' ('isa pa' = one more).
Turns a statement into a yes/no question. Goes after the first word or after short pronouns: 'Okay ka ba?' 'Tapos na ba?'

examples.en: Are you going to the party?

notes: Reports what someone else said: 'Late daw siya' = He says he'll be late. 'raw' after vowels in careful speech; 'daw' is fine casually.
'Ako din' = me too. 'rin' after vowels in careful speech ('ako rin'); casual speech uses 'din' everywhere.
Softener and limiter: 'Dito lang' = just here; 'Okay lang' = it's fine; 'Isa lang' = only one. Formal: lamang.
Shifts topic or softens: 'Ikaw naman?' = And you? 'Sige naman' = come on, please. 'Hindi naman' = not really.
Confirms or insists: 'Oo nga' = yeah, right. In requests = 'please/come on': 'Pakiabot nga.' 'Sabi ko nga' = like I said.

examples.en: Yeah, right, it really is hot.

notes: Surprise/realization: 'Ikaw pala!' = Oh, it's you! 'Oo nga pala' = Oh, by the way / that reminds me.

examples.tl: Oo nga pala, may meeting tayo bukas.
examples.en: Oh right, by the way, we have a meeting tomorrow.

notes: The everyday 'because'; also a particle that blames or explains: 'Ikaw kasi!' = It's your fault! Can start or sit inside a clause.

examples.en: I was late because of traffic.

examples.tl: Ikaw kasi, hindi ka nagbasa ng message.
examples.en: It's your fault, you didn't read the message.

notes: 'Do X first / for the time being': 'Sandali muna' = just a moment. 'Dito muna ako' = I'll stay here for now.

examples.tl: Teka muna, kukuha lang ako ng wallet.
examples.en: Wait a sec, I'll just get my wallet.

notes: Uncertainty: 'Wala yata siya' = I think he's not here. Weaker than 'siguro'. Common in texts.

examples.en: I think the bank is closed already.
I think I forgot the key.

notes: In questions = speculation: 'Uulan kaya?' = I wonder if it'll rain. Different from kaya 'so' (conj) and kaya 'can' (stress on first syllable).

examples.en: Do you think 7-Eleven is still open?

notes: Hope or unrealized wish: 'Sana okay ka' = hope you're okay; 'Pupunta sana ako' = I was going to go (but didn't). 'Sana all' = wish that were me.

examples.tl: Pupunta sana ako, kaso may trabaho.
examples.en: I would have gone, but I have work.

notes: Adds respect to elders, strangers, staff. Goes after the first word: 'Salamat po.' 'Magkano po?' 'Ho' is a softer variant. Pairs with kayo/ninyo.
Polite 'oo'. Use with elders, officials, guards, staff. 'Hindi po' for polite no.
Enclitic marking a consequence (often unwanted): 'Na-late tuloy ako' = So I ended up late. Also the verb 'to continue/go on' ('Tuloy ang party').

examples.tl: Traffic, na-late tuloy ako sa meeting.
examples.en: Traffic, so I ended up late for the meeting.

examples.tl: Tuloy pa ba ang lakad bukas?
examples.en: Is the plan tomorrow still on?

notes: 'Kahit ano man' = anything at all; 'Wala man lang' = not even one; 'Mahal man, masarap' = even if pricey, it's good.

examples.en: Not even a little gift for me?
Even if it's expensive, it's worth it.

notes: Sentence-final 'e' adds mild excuse or reluctance: 'Wala akong pera e' = I don't have money, you see. Sentence-initial 'E, ano ngayon?' = So what?

examples.tl: Hindi ako makakapunta e, may trabaho.
examples.en: I can't come, you see, I've got work.

examples.tl: E di ikaw na ang magaling.
examples.en: Well then, you're the smart one (sarcastic).

notes: 'kanin at ulam' = rice and dish. In speech, lists often use 'tapos' or 'saka' instead. Contracts to 't after vowels (formal).

examples.tl: Bumili ako ng kanin at ulam.
examples.en: I bought rice and a dish.

examples.tl: Si Ana at si Marco ang kasama ko.
examples.en: Ana and Marco are with me.

notes: The everyday 'but' (Spanish loan). 'Kaso' = 'but the problem is'. Formal 'ngunit/subalit' only in writing.

examples.en: I like it, but it's expensive.
I'll come but I'll be late.

notes: 'But' with a catch or obstacle: 'Gusto ko sana, kaso wala akong pera.' Very common in casual speech.

examples.en: The food there is good, but it's far.

examples.tl: Sasama ako, kaso may shift ako.
examples.en: I'd join, but I have a shift.

notes: Slightly more formal than kasi. 'dahil sa' + noun = because of: 'dahil sa ulan'. 'Dahil' + clause: 'dahil umulan'.

examples.tl: Na-cancel ang flight dahil sa bagyo.
examples.en: The flight was cancelled because of the typhoon.

examples.tl: Umuwi siya dahil may sakit siya.
examples.en: He/she went home because he/she was sick.

notes: Conditions and indirect questions: 'Kung gusto mo' = if you want; 'Hindi ko alam kung saan' = I don't know where. 'Kung ako sa'yo' = if I were you.

examples.tl: Hindi ko alam kung open pa sila.
examples.en: I don't know if they're still open.

notes: For future or habitual 'when': 'Kapag umulan, baha.' Spoken 'pag'. Past 'when' uses 'noong' instead.

examples.tl: Text mo ako pag nandito ka na.

en: for / so that / in order to
notes: 'para sa' + noun = for; 'para' + verb = in order to. Also 'Para!' = stop (to a jeep/bus driver). 'parang' = like/seems.

examples.tl: Umaga ako umalis para hindi ma-traffic.
examples.en: I left in the morning so I wouldn't hit traffic.

notes: Storytelling connector: 'Kumain kami, tapos nag-mall.' As adj = finished ('Tapos na'). 'Tapos?' = And then what?

examples.tl: Nag-gym ako, tapos kumain sa Poblacion.
examples.en: I went to the gym, then ate in Poblacion.

notes: 'Kape o tsaa?' Also an attention marker at sentence end: 'Eto, o!' = Here, look!

examples.en: Shall we take a Grab or a jeep?

notes: Result connector at the start of a clause: 'Umulan, kaya hindi ako umalis.' 'Kaya nga' = exactly, that's why.

examples.en: There was traffic, so I was late.
That's exactly why I told you.

notes: 'Habang naghihintay' = while waiting. 'Habang buhay' = for life. 'Habang maaga' = while it's early.

examples.tl: Kumain ako habang naghihintay ng Grab.
examples.en: I ate while waiting for the Grab.

examples.tl: Umuwi na tayo habang maaga pa.
examples.en: Let's go home while it's still early.

notes: As conjunction: 'bago umalis' = before leaving. Same word as adjective 'new'. Not 'noon/dati' (before = in the past).

examples.tl: Tumawag ka muna bago ka pumunta.

notes: 'pagkatapos ng trabaho' = after work; 'pagkatapos kumain' = after eating. Casual speech often just uses 'tapos'.

examples.en: After work, I go to the gym.

notes: 'Kahit umulan' = even if it rains. 'Kahit ano' = anything; 'kahit saan' = anywhere; 'kahit sino' = anyone.

examples.en: I'll go even if it rains.

examples.tl: Kahit ano, okay lang sa akin.

notes: Spoken 'tsaka'. Adds an item or a next step: 'Isang kape, tsaka tubig.' 'Saka na' = later / some other time.

examples.tl: Bili ka ng tinapay, tsaka itlog.

examples.en: Let's talk about it some other time.

notes: Time or place: 'hanggang bukas' = until tomorrow; 'hanggang Cubao' = as far as Cubao. 'Hanggang dito lang' = this is as far as it goes.

examples.tl: Hanggang Ayala lang ang jeep na ito.
examples.en: This jeep only goes as far as Ayala.

notes: After a negative: 'Hindi si Ana kundi si Marco' = not Ana but Marco. 'Walang iba kundi' = none other than.

examples.tl: Hindi ako kundi siya ang nagluto.
examples.en: It wasn't me but him/her who cooked.
I have nothing to do but wait.

notes: Comparison: 'mas mura kesa sa Grab' = cheaper than Grab. Standard spelling 'kaysa'; spoken 'kesa'.

examples.tl: Mas mabilis ang MRT kesa sa bus.
examples.en: The MRT is faster than the bus.

examples.tl: Mas gusto ko ang sinigang kesa adobo.

notes: Existential, directly before a noun: 'May tao' = there's someone; 'May pera ako' = I have money. Before pronouns/adverbs use 'mayroon'.
Spoken 'meron'. Used when a pronoun/particle follows ('Meron akong...') or alone as the answer 'Yes, there is.' 'Meron pa?' = Any more?

examples.en: Is there water left? There is.

en: none / there is no / not have
notes: Negative existential: 'Wala akong pera' = I have no money; 'Wala siya' = he's not here. Linker: 'walang tao'. 'Wala lang' = nothing, never mind.

examples.en: I don't have any phone credit.

notes: 'Ngayon' = right now or today. 'ngayong gabi' = tonight; 'ngayong araw' = today. Contrast with 'na' (already/now).

examples.tl: May lakad ka ba ngayong gabi?

notes: Earlier the same day. 'Kanina lang' = just now. 'Kanina pa' = for a while already (been waiting).

examples.en: I've been waiting here for a while.

notes: Later the same day. 'mamayang gabi' = tonight (later). 'Mamaya na' = later, not now. For a later day use 'sa susunod'.
Stress on first syllable. 'Bukás' (last syllable) = open. 'Bukas ng umaga' = tomorrow morning.
'Kahapon ng gabi' or 'kagabi' = last night. 'Noong isang araw' = the other day.

examples.tl: Nakita ko siya kahapon sa Greenbelt.
examples.en: I saw him/her yesterday at Greenbelt.

notes: ka- + gabi. Same pattern: 'kaninang umaga' = this morning (earlier).

examples.en: Did you go home last night?

notes: 'Lagi' and 'palagi' are interchangeable; 'lagi' is shorter and more common in speech. Linker: 'laging late'.
Same meaning as lagi, slightly more emphatic. 'Palaging' before a word it modifies.

examples.en: I always go to the gym in the morning.

notes: 'Minsan' = sometimes; 'minsan lang' = just once / rarely; 'paminsan-minsan' = once in a while.

examples.en: Sometimes I take a jeep, sometimes Grab.
I only drink once in a while.

notes: 'Madalas akong...' = I often... 'Kadalasan' = usually/most of the time.

examples.tl: Madalas ba umulan dito sa Hunyo?
examples.en: Does it often rain here in June?

notes: 'Bihira lang' = only rarely. Opposite of madalas.

examples.en: I rarely take the jeep anymore.

examples.tl: Bihira lang siyang umuwi sa probinsya.
examples.en: He/she seldom goes home to the province.

notes: Reduplication = 'every': 'gabi-gabi' = every night, 'linggo-linggo' = every week, 'buwan-buwan' = monthly.

examples.en: I go to the gym every day.
Every day there's traffic in Makati.

notes: Enclitic-like, after the verb: 'Umuwi agad' = went home right away. 'Agad-agad' = immediately (emphatic).

examples.tl: Umuwi ako agad pagkatapos ng shift.
examples.en: I went home right after my shift.

notes: 'Biglang umulan' = it suddenly rained. 'Bigla-bigla' = out of nowhere. Linker -ng: 'biglang'.
Emphasis or genuine surprise: 'Talaga?' = Really? 'Ganyan talaga' = that's really how it is.

examples.en: The sisig here is really good.

notes: Intensifier: 'sobrang mahal' = super expensive. As noun = excess/leftover: 'May sobra pa' = there's extra.

examples.tl: Sobra na ang traffic sa EDSA.
examples.en: The traffic on EDSA is too much.

notes: Softens an adjective: 'medyo mahal' = a bit pricey; 'medyo pagod' = kind of tired. Very frequent in Taglish.

examples.en: The condos there are kind of expensive.

notes: 'Masyadong mahal' = too expensive. 'Hindi masyado' = not that much. 'Masyado ka naman' = you're too much!
'Halos lahat' = almost everyone/everything; 'halos araw-araw' = almost daily. Casual alternative: 'muntik' (almost did something).

examples.tl: Halos lahat ng tindahan sarado ngayon.
examples.en: Almost all the shops are closed today.
The trip is almost an hour.

notes: Possibility, often worried: 'Baka umulan' = it might rain. Also 'baka' = cow (stress 'báka'). 'Baka naman' = maybe, hopefully.

examples.en: I might be late, because of traffic.

examples.tl: Baka wala na siya sa office.
examples.en: He/she might not be at the office anymore.

notes: More confident than 'baka'. 'Siguro nga' = I suppose so. 'Oo siguro' = yeah, probably. From Spanish seguro.
Casual yes (two syllables: o-o). Polite: 'opo'. 'Oo nga' = yeah, right. 'Oo naman' = of course.
Negates verbs/adjectives: 'Hindi masarap.' Casual 'di'. Use 'wala' for 'none/not have'. Polite 'hindi po'.
Negative command. Spoken 'wag'. 'Huwag na' = no need / don't bother. 'Wag kang...' = don't you...
Opposite of gusto. Takes ng/ko: 'Ayaw ko' = I don't want to; 'Ayaw ko ng gulay' = I don't like vegetables. 'Ayaw ko na' = I quit.

examples.en: He/she doesn't want to come along.

notes: Pseudo-verb with ng-pronouns: 'Gusto ko' = I want/like; 'Gusto mo ba?' = Do you want? 'Gusto kita' = I like you.

examples.tl: Gusto mo bang sumama sa Tagaytay?
examples.en: Do you want to come to Tagaytay?

notes: Permission/possibility: 'Pwede ba?' = Is it okay? 'Pwede na' = good enough. Standard spelling 'puwede'.
Pseudo-verb: 'Kailangan ko ng...' = I need...; 'Kailangan umalis' = need to leave. Spoken 'kelangan'.

examples.en: I need to go home early.

notes: 'Dapat kang magpahinga' = you should rest. 'Dapat sana' = should have. 'Dapat lang' = as it should be / serves you right.

examples.tl: Dapat sana nag-Grab na lang tayo.
examples.en: We should have just taken a Grab.

notes: Stress on FIRST syllable (unlike kayâ 'so/I wonder'). 'Kaya ko' = I can handle it. 'Kaya mo yan!' = You can do it!

examples.tl: Hindi ko kayang maglakad hanggang Ayala.
examples.en: I can't manage to walk all the way to Ayala.

notes: All-purpose agreement and closing: 'Sige, bye.' 'Sige na' = come on / go on. 'Sige lang' = go ahead, it's fine.
'Ewan ko' = I don't know. 'Ewan ko sa'yo' = I give up on you (exasperated). 'Hindi ko alam' is the neutral form.

examples.tl: Ewan ko kung open pa sila.
examples.en: I don't know if they're still open.

notes: Tag question seeking agreement; texted 'diba'. 'Di ba?' alone = Right? Told you!
From Spanish siempre (always) but means 'of course'. Texted 'syempre'. 'Siyempre naman' = but of course.

examples.en: Of course, I'm joining the meal.
Of course it's expensive, that's BGC.

notes: Hedging and comparison: 'Parang uulan' = looks like rain; 'parang kape' = like coffee. Extremely common filler in Taglish.

examples.en: I think I'm kind of hungry.

notes: 'Ulit' after the verb: 'Sabihin mo ulit' = say it again. Also 'Ulit?' = Again? 'Muli' is formal.
Past habit or former state: 'Dati, mura ang pamasahe.' 'dating' = former/ex ('dating boss ko').

examples.tl: Dati, naglalakad lang ako papuntang office.
examples.en: Before, I used to just walk to the office.

notes: 'Saglit lang' = just a moment. 'Sandali' is the same. 'Teka' = wait (from hintay ka).

examples.tl: Saglit lang, kukunin ko yung wallet ko.
examples.en: Just a sec, I'll get my wallet.

notes: Makes comparatives: 'mas mura' = cheaper; 'mas gusto ko' = I prefer. Pair with 'kesa (sa)' = than.

examples.tl: Mas mura ang jeep kesa sa Grab.
examples.en: The jeep is cheaper than Grab.

examples.tl: Mas gusto ko ang mainit na kape.

notes: Prefix for superlatives: 'pinakamura' = cheapest; 'pinakamasarap' = tastiest. Often 'ang pinaka-' + adj.
ma- + ganda. Also 'good' in greetings: 'Magandang umaga.' For people, 'maganda' = pretty (fem.); 'gwapo' = handsome.

examples.tl: Maganda ang view sa condo mo.
examples.en: The view from your condo is beautiful.

notes: 'Mabuti naman' = I'm fine (reply to kumusta). 'Buti na lang' = good thing that... 'Buti pa' = better off.

examples.tl: Buti na lang may dala akong payong.
examples.en: Good thing I brought an umbrella.

notes: Two meanings: expensive ('Mahal ang Grab') and love/dear ('Mahal kita', 'mahal ko' = my love).

examples.tl: Ang mahal ng rent sa BGC!
examples.en: Rent in BGC is so expensive!

notes: 'Mura lang' = it's cheap. 'Pamura' / 'murang-mura' = very cheap. 'Mura' (stress murá) also = curse word.

examples.tl: Mura lang ang pagkain sa carinderia.
examples.en: Food at the carinderia is cheap.
It's cheaper if you pay cash.

notes: ma- + laki. 'Malaking bahay' (linker -ng). 'Malaki ang discount' = big discount.

examples.en: The mall in Ortigas is big.

notes: ma- + liit. 'Maliit lang' = it's just small. 'Maliit na studio' = a small studio unit.

examples.tl: Maliit lang ang unit ko, studio type.
examples.en: My unit is just small, studio type.

notes: 'Malayo pa' = still far. 'Malayo-layo' = quite far. 'Gaano kalayo?' = how far?

examples.tl: Malayo ang airport mula sa Makati.
examples.en: The airport is far from Makati.

notes: 'Malapit lang' = just nearby. 'Malapit na' = almost there / coming soon. 'malapit sa' = near to.

examples.tl: Malapit lang ang gym sa condo ko.
examples.en: The gym is just near my condo.

notes: 'Mabilis lang' = it's quick. 'Bilisan mo' = hurry up. 'Dali' is also used for 'quick!'.

examples.tl: Mabilis ang MRT kung walang aberya.
examples.en: The MRT is fast if there's no glitch.

examples.tl: Mabilis lang ang process sa bangko.
examples.en: The process at the bank was quick.

notes: 'Mabagal ang internet' = the internet is slow. 'Bagal' alone as complaint: 'Bagal!'
ma- + sarap. 'Sarap!' alone = yum. Also for pleasant feelings: 'masarap matulog' = it's nice to sleep.

examples.tl: Ang sarap ng tulog ko kagabi.
examples.en: I slept so well last night.

notes: Weather, food, drink. 'Ang init!' = It's so hot! 'Mainit ang ulo' = short-tempered. Spicy is 'maanghang'.

examples.tl: Sobrang init sa labas, mag-aircon tayo.
examples.en: It's so hot outside, let's get some aircon.

examples.tl: Gusto ko ng mainit na kape.

notes: 'Malamig na tubig' = cold water. 'Ang lamig!' = So cold! Tagaytay/Baguio are 'malamig'.

examples.en: It's cold in Baguio in December.

notes: 'Bagong phone' = new phone (linker -ng). 'Bago lang' = brand new / just recently. Also the conjunction 'before'.

examples.en: There's a new restaurant in Salcedo.

notes: For objects only. Old PEOPLE = 'matanda'. 'Lumang building' = old building.

examples.tl: Lumang building yun pero maganda pa.
examples.en: That's an old building but still nice.

notes: 'Madali lang' = it's easy. Related 'dali' = hurry ('Dali!' = quick!). 'Madaling araw' = early morning/dawn.

examples.tl: Madali lang pumunta dun, isang jeep lang.
examples.en: It's easy to get there, just one jeep.

notes: Two meanings: difficult ('mahirap ang exam') and poor ('mahirap na pamilya'). 'Hirap' alone = it's a struggle.

examples.en: It's hard to drive in Manila.

examples.tl: Mahirap makahanap ng Grab kapag umuulan.
examples.en: It's hard to find a Grab when it's raining.

notes: 'Maraming tao' = lots of people. 'Ang dami!' = So many! 'Maraming salamat' = thank you very much.

examples.en: There are lots of people in Divisoria.

notes: Standard 'kaunti'; spoken 'konti'. 'Konti lang' = just a little. 'Konting-konti' = very little.

examples.tl: Konti lang ang pera ko ngayon.
examples.en: I only have a little money right now.

notes: Containers, vehicles, venues: 'Puno ang jeep' = the jeep is full. Stressed 'púno' = tree. Full stomach = 'busog'.

examples.tl: Puno na ang MRT, next train na lang.
examples.en: The MRT is full, let's take the next train.

notes: Fully adopted. 'Okay lang' = it's fine / I'm fine. 'Okay na' = it's good now. 'Okay ka lang?' = you alright?

examples.tl: Okay lang ba kung late ako ng konti?
examples.en: Is it okay if I'm a little late?
It's okay now, I've paid it.

notes: 'Ayos lang' = it's fine. 'Ayos!' = nice, great! 'Ayusin mo' = fix it. 'Maayos' = well-arranged, going well.

examples.tl: Ayos! Approved na ang leave ko.

notes: People or events: 'Masaya ako' = I'm happy; 'Masaya ang party' = the party was fun. 'Ang saya!' = so fun!

examples.en: Christmas in the Philippines is fun.

notes: People or places/moods. 'Nalulungkot ako' = I'm feeling sad. 'Ang lungkot' = how sad.

examples.tl: Malungkot siya kasi umalis ang kaibigan niya.
examples.en: He/she is sad because their friend left.

examples.tl: Malungkot ang condo kapag mag-isa ka.
examples.en: The condo is lonely when you're alone.

notes: 'Pagod na ako' = I'm tired already. 'Nakakapagod' = tiring. 'Pahinga' = rest.
'Gutom na ako' = I'm hungry. 'Nagugutom ako' (verb form) is also common. 'Gutom ka ba?' = hungry?
Full after eating. 'Busog na ako' = I'm full. Not 'puno' (that's for containers). 'Nakakabusog' = filling.
ma- + linis. 'Maglinis' = to clean. Opposite: 'madumi'. 'Malinis ang CR' = the restroom is clean.

examples.tl: Malinis ang CR sa mall na ito.
examples.en: The restrooms in this mall are clean.

notes: Spoken 'madumi'; formal 'marumi'. 'Dumi' = dirt. 'Madumi ang tubig' = the water is dirty.

examples.tl: Madumi ang sapatos ko dahil sa baha.
examples.en: My shoes are dirty because of the flood.
The table is still dirty, please clean it.

notes: Height or amount: 'mataas ang presyo' = prices are high; 'mataas na building' = tall building. Tall person = 'matangkad'.
'Mababa ang presyo' = low price. 'Mababang grade' = low grade. Short person = 'maliit' or 'pandak' (casual).

examples.tl: Mababa ang sweldo pero okay ang work.
examples.en: The salary is low but the work is fine.

notes: For people and pets. 'Mabait siya' = he/she is nice. 'Ang bait!' = so kind! Opposite: 'masama' or 'salbahe'.

examples.tl: Mabait ang guard sa building namin.
examples.en: The guard in our building is nice.

notes: 'Masama ang panahon' = the weather is bad. 'Masama ang pakiramdam ko' = I feel sick. 'Masamang balita' = bad news.

examples.en: Traffic is bad when it rains.

notes: 'Tama!' = Correct! 'Tama ka' = you're right. 'Tama na' = that's enough, stop. 'Tama lang' = just right.
'Mali ako' = I was wrong. 'Mali yung address' = the address is wrong. 'Nagkamali ako' = I made a mistake.

examples.tl: Mali yung address na binigay ko sa Grab.
examples.en: The address I gave to Grab was wrong.

examples.tl: Mali ka, Linggo ang flight, hindi Sabado.
examples.en: You're wrong, the flight is Sunday, not Saturday.

notes: 'Sira ang aircon' = the aircon is broken. 'Nasira' = got broken. 'Sira-ulo' = crazy (slang).

examples.tl: Sira ang elevator, hagdan muna tayo.
examples.en: The elevator is broken, let's take the stairs for now.

examples.tl: Nasira ang phone ko sa ulan.
examples.en: My phone got damaged in the rain.

notes: Formal; most Manileños just say 'busy'. Common in 'Sorry sa abala' = sorry for the bother/inconvenience.

examples.tl: Sorry sa abala, pwede bang magtanong?
examples.en: Sorry to bother you, can I ask something?

examples.tl: Abala siya ngayon, busy sa trabaho.
examples.en: He/she is busy right now, busy with work.
